data.name: Vishvamitra
data.gender_notes: Vishvamitra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: He who pervades all. The name Vishvamitra carries the meaning “All-pervading” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Tamil. Parents who choose Vishvamitra usually hope their child will grow to embody all-pervading and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Vishvamitra belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “All-pervading.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishvamitra total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

celebrity_usage: Vishvamitra was a sage, a priest, and a warrior in Hindu mythology, who was a mentor to the prince Rama, the hero of the Ramayana.
data.cultural_impact: Vishvamitra is an ancient sage and a great Rishi (seer or listener) in Hindu mythology, revered for his immense wisdom and knowledge of chants or mantras, which have the power to evoke the gods and manage the elements of nature. He is known for composing the famous 'Atharva Veda' – the last and most mystical of the four Vedas. Vishvamitra has also played an instrumental role in both the Ramayana and Mahabharata epics. In the Ramayana, he was the guru (teacher) of King Dasharatha and arranged for his sons to marry Rama, Lakshmana, and Bharata. In the Mahabharata, he incarnated as Vyasa's charioteer and teacher and implemented the strategy for the Kurukshetra war between the Pandavas and Kauravas.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Vishvamitra" signifies the all-pervading consciousness and wisdom that transcends the limits of the individual self and merges with the entire universe. Vishvamitra represents the capacity to embody and radiate that cosmic knowledge and consciousness that exists within us all. His story is a reminder of the transformative power of wisdom, knowledge, and dedication, and the importance of striving to understand the deeper spiritual truths of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vishvamitra: The all-pervading sage, possessing universal knowledge and wisdom. His name signifies one who has conquered the universe with his intellect and devotion.

historical_references.reference: Vishvamitra was a sage and a king in ancient India. He was a descendant of the lunar dynasty and was a pupil of the sage Jamadagni. Vishvamitra's wife was Shakuntala, who bore him a son named Shakuni. Vishvamitra is best known for performing the 'Ashwamedha Yagna', the horse sacrifice, for King Janaka of Videha to establish his royal sovereignty.

Vishvamitra is also known as the composer of the 'Vishvamitra Samhita', which is a part of the 'Atharva Veda'. This text outlines various rituals, mantras and hymns for various deities. It is believed that Vishvamitra was a highly learned sage and had mastery over various forms of knowledge including astronomy, mathematics and music.
historical_references.context: Later Vedic period, Indian spirituality and literature

modern_usage.modern_context: Vishvamitra, an ancient sage and seer in Hindu mythology, has found modern relevance across various platforms. Netflix recently released a show titled 'Vishvamitra' that retells the legend of the sage through a contemporary lens. In the comic book world, Mangamekka features a comic series based on Vishvamitra's life and adventures. Lastly, Wikipedia has numerous pages dedicated to Vishvamitra, providing information on his mythological background, historical significance, and various interpretations.
